entries.title: Nested-event displays use the wrong interval and reversed probability endpoints
entries.locator: arXiv:2107.09838v2, proof of Lemma3.2 following Proposition3.3 (printed p.8), and Proposition3.9 (printed p.10). Versioned HTML and extracted PDF text compared17 November2026; no visual-PDF or journal comparison.
entries.claim: For ai<=an the interval-product chain displays the larger interval [0,an] as the intersection, then identifies it with fi. Proposition3.9 assumes 1<=alpha1<=...<=alphan<=0.
entries.problem: The intersection is [0,ai], and the displayed endpoint chain has no solutions. For example, ai=1/4 and an=3/4 give a product indicator of [0,1/4], not [0,3/4]. The intended ordered strip probabilities lie between zero and one.
entries.correction: Use fi fn=indicator[0,ai]=fi and 0<=alpha1<=...<=alphan<=1. AFJX proves the resulting nested-event product formula directly. L3SC uses this formula at the constant-grid minimizer. These local display corrections preserve the main all-order square and rectangle conclusions.
entries.leanImpact: State interval intersection with the minimum endpoint and give the nested probability parameters a nonempty ordered range in[0,1]. Do not formalize the reversed endpoint chain as a vacuous theorem. The written replacement is independently derived; no compiled association or source confirmation is claimed.

resolution.summary: Correct the nested intersection and the direction of the endpoint chain.
resolution.impact: Local display corrections; the all-order square and rectangle conclusions are unchanged.
